title: Global burden of bacterial AMR (WHO 2024)
summary: Bacterial AMR directly caused ~1.27 million deaths in 2019; India is among high-burden countries. Stewardship programs reduce inappropriate broad-spectrum use.
clinical_lesson: Empirical fluoroquinolone use for UTI is often inappropriate in India due to high E. coli FQ resistance (ICMR/GLASS patterns >65% non-susceptibility in many centers).
intervention: WHO AWaRe classification + local antibiogram-guided empiric therapy
outcome: National AMR action plans mandate hospital AMS; tools must use local susceptibility data.

title: ICMR AMR Surveillance Network — Indian hospital patterns
summary: ICMR network surveillance shows rising carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella and high fluoroquinolone resistance in Enterobacterales from outpatient UTI isolates.
clinical_lesson: For uncomplicated UTI in India, nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin often preferred over ciprofloxacin when susceptibility supports; carbapenems reserved for ESBL/CRE.
intervention: Antibiogram-driven formulary restrictions + AMS pharmacist review
outcome: Published network reports guide empirical therapy by region and specimen type.
source: ICMR AMRSN / Indian Journal of Medical Research surveillance summaries

title: Antimicrobial stewardship programs — Core Elements (CDC/IDSA)
setting: US hospitals (model applicable to JIPMER pilot)
summary: Seven core elements: leadership, accountability, drug expertise, action, tracking, reporting, education. Decision support must remain physician-directed.
clinical_lesson: CDS tools increase Access-tier use when integrated with pharmacy-led review — not autonomous prescribing.
intervention: Prospective audit and feedback + pre-prescription authorization for restricted agents
outcome: Meta-analyses show 10–20% reduction in antimicrobial consumption without worsening mortality when ASP implemented.
source: CDC Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship Programs (2023 update)

title: IDSA UTI Guidelines — uncomplicated cystitis
summary: First-line: nitrofurantoin 100mg BD x 5 days, TMP-SMX DS BD x 3 days (if local resistance <20%), or fosfomycin 3g single dose. FQ not first-line due resistance.
clinical_lesson: Match empiric choice to local susceptibility; duration 5–7 days uncomplicated.
outcome: Reduced recurrence and resistance selection pressure vs broad FQ use.
source: Gupta K et al. IDSA UTI Guidelines 2010 (still referenced; EAU 2024 updates similar principles)

title: Hospital AMS Pilot — target case (your pilot fills real numbers)
setting: Any tertiary-care hospital — proposed 4-week research pilot
summary: Deploy AMRShield with institution WHONET antibiogram upload. Measure Access-tier empiric recommendations, audit FLAG rate, and pharmacist review time.
clinical_lesson: Replace reference surveillance data with your hospital's organism-specific susceptibility in Week 1.
intervention: AMRShield CDS + physician attestation + weekly AMS committee report
outcome: Target KPIs: ≥60% Access-tier empirics for uncomplicated UTI; 100% physician sign-off; zero PHI to cloud AI.
source: AMRShield pilot protocol — pending local ethics approval

title: Purulent SSTI — MRSA coverage when risk factors present
summary: Indian tertiary centers report MRSA proportions ~25–40% in S. aureus from skin/soft tissue in many studies. TMP-SMX, clindamycin, or doxycycline for outpatient; vancomycin if severe/systemic.
clinical_lesson: Do not use vancomycin monotherapy for uncomplicated cellulitis without MRSA risk or culture data.
intervention: Risk-stratify MRSA; use local MRSA antibiogram
outcome: Avoid unnecessary glycopeptide use; de-escalate when culture returns MSSA.
source: IDSA SSTI Guidelines 2014; Indian MRSA prevalence literature (tertiary care meta-analyses)
